Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
105 AM PST Wed Nov 25 2026

.SYNOPSIS...24/115 PM.

Warming temperatures and dry weather is expected most of the week
due to a predominant offshore flow pattern. Temperatures will 
peak on Thanksgiving and Friday with some gusty northeast winds at
times, then cooling will begin over the weekend. There is a 
possibility of a large storm system around the middle of next 
week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-FRI)...25/104 AM.

Current radar/satellite shows the decaying cold front is
progressing as expected. A few showers will likely reach
the Central coast early this morning. Local amounts under 
0.05" & elsewhere zero measurable precipition is expected. 

Offshore pressure gradients from the N and E will increase
through the Day Wednesday. Wind speeds will generally respond 
across the usual Santa Ana favored areas across LA/VTA counties. 
Gradients will peak on Thursday, LAX-DAG -5 mb & LAX-BFL -6.5 mb. 
This will result in a significant north wind component which is
atypical of traditional Santa wind events - meaning stronger
northerly winds into LA Valleys and less wind across western 
parts of Ventura county.

Have proactively issued wind advisories for Santa Susanna and
western San Gabriel Mtns. The day shift will likely expand
to cover Santa Monica mtns and some valley locations of LA/VTA
such as Santa Clarita, San Fernando, and Simi Valleys. 

Gradients will begin to trend onshore for Friday (esp LAX-DAG)
but will remain weak to moderately offshore. Thus, gusty winds
are expected Friday morning butchances for wind advisories are
much lower. However, downsloping will overlap with peaking 500mb
heights (588-590dm) resulting in the warmest day with temperatures
in the mid 80s across the LA valleys. 

The biggest concern this week will be at the beaches where the 
combination of very high tides & surf will result in a significant
threat for coastal flooding especially Today and Tomorrow. 
Please refer to LAXCFWLOX and beaches section for more information.

.LONG TERM (SAT-TUE)...25/104 AM.

The ridge is expected to break down and shift east this weekend 
in response to the next storm system moving into the PACNW. This 
will result in cooler temperatures near seasonal norms by Sunday. 
Another storm system will mainly impact northern California but 
the tail end of the storm will likely drop some light rain across 
our area Sunday night into Monday. Rain amounts are projected to 
be mostly under 0.5".

A stronger storm system is likely Tuesday into Wednesday. There
is some reasonable concern from a hydrological standpoint since
this system will tap into subtropical moisture. EPS has a 120+
knot jet streak off the Central Coast and EPS/GEFS IVT forecasts
fall into the 300-400 range - which is a solid weak atmospheric
river. About 25% of ensemble members show a moderate strength AR.
This combined with the very anomalous, record-breaking SSTs does
raise eyebrows considering the high rainfall rates we have already
had with previous systems. Current guidance suggests widespread 
amounts of at least 1-2 inches with upslope areas as high as 5 
inches in a 6-8 hour period. Likely to be some thunderstorm risk.
Snow levels would likely be above 8000 ft.

&&

.AVIATION...25/0558Z.

At 0522Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

For KSMX, KSBP, and KPRB, there is a 30% chance of -SHRA and/or 
MVFR CIGs from 10Z-15Z Wed. There is also a 30% chance of LIFR 
conditions developing from 10Z-18Z Wed. Otherwise, VFR conditions
are expected at all other sites through the forecast period.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Good confidence that any east
wind component remains below 7 kts. 

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF. No wind issues expected.

&&

.MARINE...24/948 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate confidence in current forecast. 
Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level seas should arrive tonight, with
areas of SCA level winds developing Wednesday morning. SCA level
seas with areas of SCA level winds are expected through Friday. 
During this time period, seas will peak between 14 and 19 feet on
Wednesday. Good chance for localized SCA level NE winds Thursday
into Friday. For Friday night through Sunday, high confidence in 
winds remaining below SCA levels, but there is a 50-70% chance of 
SCA level seas continuing.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate confidence in 
current forecast. SCA level seas develop tonight, lasting into
Friday. SCA level winds are expected at times, especially Thursday
into Friday. Seas will peak between 13 and 17 feet on Wednesday. 
For Friday night through Sunday, high confidence in winds 
remaining below SCA levels, but a 40-60% chance of SCA level seas 
continuing. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through tonight, high confidence
in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For Wednesday
through Thursday, high confidence in SCA level winds, specifically
across the western half of the Santa Barbara Channel on Wednesday
and from Point Mugu to Santa Monica on Thursday. Additionally,
there is a 40-60% chance of widespread SCA level seas Wednesday
through Thursday. For Friday through Sunday, winds and seas are
expected to remain below SCA for most areas. The only exception
will be the western half of the Santa Barbara Channel with a 50%
chance of SCA level winds Sunday afternoon and evening. 

A large, west long period swell will create hazardous boating
conditions for the coastal waters, by creating large breaking 
waves near coastlines and harbor entrances. These waves can 
capsize small vessels. Follow guidance from local officials.

&&

.BEACHES...24/950 PM.

A large, long period, west swell will move into the coastal
waters, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. This large swell will 
combine with very high tides to bring large surf to the area as 
well as moderate to significant coastal flooding.

The highest surf and most significant coastal flooding issues are
expected across the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, as
well as the Ventura County coastline, and far eastern portions of
the southern Santa Barbara County coasts. Elsewhere, the surf and
coastal flooding issues are a bit less, but still concerning. High
tide will be the timing of greatest concern for coastal flooding,
and low lying coastal areas with no protection from the ocean will
be more vulnerable. Coastal structures are at an increased risk 
for damage. There will be many, strong rip currently nearly 
everywhere, strong long shore currents, a risk of sneaker waves, 
large shore pound, coastal erosion. These conditions will lead to
an increased risk of drowning and make swimming dangerous. 

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories and warnings in effect.
